title: Fixed-object free-arrow pushouts compute variable-object attachments
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, the two-object categories $U(K)$ and the fixed-object categories $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], and the free-arrow functors of [lem-coef-fixed-object-free-arrow-adjunction]. Let $O$ be a small set, $a,b\in O$ (possibly equal), $i:K\to L$ any map of small simplicial sets, $C\in\mathrm{sCat}_O$, and $h:K\to C(a,b)$ a simplicial map. Let $\bar h:F^O_{a,b}(K)\to C$ be its adjunct and let $h_U:U(K)\to C$ send $0,1$ to $a,b$ with arrow map $h$. Form the pushout
$$P=C\amalg_{F^O_{a,b}(K)}F^O_{a,b}(L)$$
in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$. The canonical functor $U(L)\to F^O_{a,b}(L)\to P$, together with $C\to P$, exhibits $P$ as the pushout $C\amalg_{U(K)}U(L)$ in the category $\mathrm{sCat}$ allowing arbitrary object functions. In particular this variable-object pushout has object set canonically $O$. More precisely, for every small simplicial category $T$, restriction induces a bijection between functors $P\to T$ and pairs $(G,\ell)$ consisting of a simplicial functor $G:C\to T$ and a map $\ell:L\to T(Ga,Gb)$ satisfying $\ell i=G_{a,b}h$. This bijection commutes with postcomposition in $T$ and restricts to any prescribed object function $O\to\operatorname{Ob}T$. No injectivity condition on $i$, distinctness of $a,b$, or Kan condition is assumed.

source.place: Bergner, A model category structure on the category of simplicial categories, Lemma 3.4, horn case, printed p.11: comparison with the fixed-object pushout. Agent makes its implicit comparison precise for coincident attaching objects and arbitrary simplicial maps; no Stacks tag states this enriched pushout comparison.

proof.text: Write $j:C\to P$ and $v:F^O_{a,b}(L)\to P$ for the fixed-object pushout maps. Its existence is supplied by the cocompleteness of the fixed-object model category in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. For $M=K,L$, define $e_M:U(M)\to F^O_{a,b}(M)$ by $0\mapsto a$, $1\mapsto b$ and by sending each simplex of $M$ to its length-one word. This preserves identities and composition: in $U(M)$ no two nonidentity arrows are composable, even when their images are loops. The word construction and adjunction of [lem-coef-fixed-object-free-arrow-adjunction] give $F(i)e_K=e_LU(i)$ and $\bar h e_K=h_U$, by checking objects and the displayed arrow maps. Therefore $j h_U=v e_L U(i)$, so $(j,v e_L)$ is a cocone on the variable-object span. Pushout means the colimit of this three-object span as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Lemma 3.4, horn case, printed p.11; agent supplies the canonical cocone and allows equal endpoints

proof.text: Fix a small target $T$ and an object function $f:O\to\operatorname{Ob}T$. Define an $O$-object simplicial category $T_f$ by $T_f(x,y)=T(fx,fy)$, with identities and composition those of $T$. The category laws are exactly the corresponding laws in $T$. There is a simplicial functor $q_f:T_f\to T$ with object function $f$ and identity mapping-set maps. For any $D\in\mathrm{sCat}_O$, a functor $D\to T$ with object function $f$ is exactly an identity-on-$O$ functor $D\to T_f$: both specify the same maps $D(x,y)\to T(fx,fy)$ with the same identity and composition equations. These assignments are inverse simply by retaining the mapping-set maps. These are the definitions of simplicial category and functor in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. In particular nothing requires $f$ to be injective.

source.place: Section 1 definitions, printed pp.1-3; explicit reindexing of a target category supplied by the agent

proof.text: Given $(G,\ell)$ in the statement with object function $f$, view $G$ as $G_f:C\to T_f$ by step 2. The adjunction [lem-coef-fixed-object-free-arrow-adjunction] turns $\ell$ into $w:F^O_{a,b}(L)\to T_f$. The two functors $G_f\bar h$ and $wF(i)$ out of $F^O_{a,b}(K)$ correspond respectively to $G_{a,b}h$ and $\ell i$, by the stated naturality of the adjunction in both variables. Thus they agree. The fixed-object pushout property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives a unique $\widetilde E:P\to T_f$ with $\widetilde E j=G_f$ and $\widetilde E v=w$. Set $E=q_f\widetilde E$. It has object function $f$, satisfies $Ej=G$, and restricts to $\ell$ on the length-one generators in the $L$-leg. Conversely any $E':P\to T$ with these restrictions has object function $f$, since $j$ is identity on $O$. Viewed in $T_f$, its restriction along $v$ must equal $w$ by the same adjunction, and its restriction along $j$ is $G_f$. Uniqueness in the fixed-object pushout forces $E'=E$. Hence restriction is a bijection for each prescribed $f$; ranging over all $f$ gives precisely the asserted bijection for arbitrary enriched functors.

source.place: Lemma 3.4, horn case, printed p.11; explicit universal-property proof of the fixed/variable-object comparison

proof.text: By the definition of $U$ in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], a functor $H:U(L)\to T$ is exactly two objects $t_0,t_1$ and a simplicial map $L\to T(t_0,t_1)$: its maps on the identity mapping sets are forced to be identities, and on the empty reverse mapping set there is only one map. The equation $H U(i)=G h_U$ forces $t_0=Ga$, $t_1=Gb$ on objects, and says exactly $\ell i=G_{a,b}h$ on the only nonidentity mapping set. Thus the compatible cocones from the variable-object span are exactly the pairs of step 3. The existence and uniqueness there is the colimit property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], so the cocone of step 1 is a pushout in $\mathrm{sCat}$. Its vertex $P$ has object set $O$ by construction in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$. Any other chosen pushout is uniquely isomorphic to it preserving the two structure maps; on objects this identifies its object set canonically with $O$.

source.place: Lemma 3.4, horn case, printed p.11, and Section 1 definition of U on printed p.3; unpacking the pushout property

proof.text: Finally let $S:T\to T'$ be any simplicial functor. If $E:P\to T$ corresponds to $(G,\ell)$, restriction of $SE$ is $(SG,S_{Ga,Gb}\ell)$, since restriction is precomposition with $j$ and with the $L$-generator map. The equality $(S_{Ga,Gb}\ell)i=(SG)_{a,b}h$ follows by applying $S_{Ga,Gb}$ to the original equality. Thus postcomposition commutes with the bijection and, by its uniqueness, with its inverse. Its object function changes from $f$ to $(\operatorname{Ob}S)f$, which proves the prescribed-object-function compatibility as well. All constructions used literal maps and equalities, not horn fillers or monomorphisms. They apply to arbitrary $i$, to $a=b$, and without any Kan hypotheses.
